title.en: Explain a custom to a visitor
title.es: Explicar una costumbre a un visitante

es: Explicar una costumbre familiar a un visitante con generalizaciones matizadas, un ejemplo concreto y una comparación respetuosa.

teaching.en: In my family, Sunday lunch is a custom: relatives tend to arrive around noon.
teaching.es: En mi familia, el almuerzo del domingo es una costumbre: los parientes suelen llegar hacia el mediodía.
teaching.explanationEs: Se presenta la costumbre y se matiza con tend to.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que compara dos costumbres con respeto.

choices.text: In other countries people eat badly; in mine we are right.
In some countries people eat separately; in mine we tend to share.
Your custom is strange, and ours is normal.

feedback.es: Solo la frase que contrasta sin juzgar respeta ambas costumbres; las otras juzgan.

hint.es: Busca la frase que contrasta sin juzgar ni decir quién tiene razón.

prompt.es: Completa: «En algunos países el visitante se quita los zapatos; en el mío no.»

feedback.es: Whereas conecta dos costumbres opuestas sin valorarlas.

hint.es: Es el conector que contrasta dos costumbres: «mientras que».

origin.text: In some countries the visitor takes off his shoes, ___ in mine he keeps them on.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con su función al explicar una costumbre.

feedback.es: Cada expresión cumple un paso: matizar, ilustrar o generalizar con cuidado.

hint.es: Piensa en qué paso de la explicación ayuda cada expresión.

prompt.es: Escucha a la hablante y elige cómo compara las costumbres.

choices.text: She says her family is better than the others.
She criticises people who eat earlier.
She compares the customs without saying which is better.

feedback.es: Contrasta dos horarios y «Neither way is better, just different» confirma que no hay juicio.

origin.audio: In my family we eat lunch at two, and in many countries people eat earlier. Neither way is better, just different.

prompt.es: Elige la generalización matizada sobre las visitas en la familia de Sara.

choices.text: Visitors tend to stay for dinner.
All visitors always stay for dinner.
No visitor ever stays for dinner.

feedback.es: Tend to expresa una tendencia; all… always y no… ever son absolutos.

origin.text: Sara explains her family's habits to a visitor.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los visitantes son bienvenidos en cualquier momento.»

answer.text: Visitors are welcome to join us at any time
accepted: Visitors are welcome to join us at any time
At any time visitors are welcome to join us

feedback.es: Welcome to + verbo indica que se invita a hacer algo: welcome to join us.

prompt.es: Explica una costumbre de tu familia a un visitante con matices y una comparación.

answer.text: In my family, Sunday lunch is a custom that we have had for many years. By and large, relatives tend to arrive around noon, and a visitor is always welcome to join us. For example, last week my cousin brought a friend from Japan, and we simply added one more chair. We usually share one big dish from the centre of the table. In some countries people eat from separate plates, whereas in mine we like to pass the food around. Neither way is better; each tradition makes sense at home. It may seem unusual at first, but visitors quickly feel at home because everybody talks, laughs and asks questions. I hope you will join us one Sunday, and I promise to explain every custom with a smile.
accepted: In my family, Sunday lunch is a custom that we have had for many years. By and large, relatives tend to arrive around noon, and a visitor is always welcome to join us. For example, last week my cousin brought a friend from Japan, and we simply added one more chair. We usually share one big dish from the centre of the table. In some countries people eat from separate plates, whereas in mine we like to pass the food around. Neither way is better; each tradition makes sense at home. It may seem unusual at first, but visitors quickly feel at home because everybody talks, laughs and asks questions. I hope you will join us one Sunday, and I promise to explain every custom with a smile.

Every Friday my family has pizza night, a tradition we started when I was a child. As a rule, everybody is home by seven, and the children tend to choose what we eat. For instance, my little brother always asks for cheese and tomato, and we all laugh. Visitors are welcome too, and they usually bring a dessert. In other countries families often eat at the table, whereas in mine we sit on the sofa and watch a film. Neither way is wrong; it is simply a different habit. At first it may feel a bit strange, but guests normally relax after the first bite. I would love to have you with us one Friday, and I promise to share the best part.

feedback.es: El texto presenta la costumbre, matiza dos generalizaciones, da un ejemplo concreto y compara con respeto.

origin.text: Explica a un visitante extranjero una costumbre de tu familia (por ejemplo, el almuerzo del domingo o la cena del viernes). Escribe unas 120–200 palabras en inglés con dos generalizaciones matizadas (tend to, by and large…), un ejemplo concreto y una comparación respetuosa con otra costumbre.

prompt.es: Elige la explicación más respetuosa de una costumbre para un visitante.

choices.text: Eating late is the right way to live.
We tend to eat late, but many families eat earlier.
Early dinners are a mistake.

feedback.es: Matiza con tend to y reconoce otras costumbres; las otras dos juzgan como si solo una fuera correcta.

origin.text: A visitor asks why your family eats so late.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el ejemplo concreto que da la hablante.

choices.text: She gives a gift to every person there.
She waves from the door and does not come in.
She gives a kiss to every person there.

feedback.es: Después de For example, la hablante cuenta que su tía besa a todos los presentes: ese es el ejemplo concreto.

origin.audio: In my family we greet everybody with a kiss. For example, when my aunt arrives, she kisses every person in the room, even the dog.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ninguna costumbre es mejor que la otra.»

answer.text: Neither custom is better than the other

feedback.es: Neither + nombre + is better than the other compara dos cosas sin elegir una.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que introduce un ejemplo concreto de la costumbre.

choices.text: For instance, we all sit on the floor.
Whereas we all sit on the floor.
By and large we all sit on the floor.

feedback.es: For instance abre un caso concreto; whereas contrasta con otra costumbre y by and large generaliza.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hemos tenido esta costumbre durante muchos años.»

feedback.es: Con una duración (many years) se usa for, no since.

origin.text: We have had this custom ___ many years.

prompt.es: Escucha la frase y elige su función.

choices.text: It is a rule with no exceptions.
It is a cautious generalisation.
It is a personal complaint.

feedback.es: By and large y tend to convierten la frase en una generalización prudente que admite excepciones.

origin.audio: By and large, visitors tend to bring a small dessert.
